name: document
title: Document
description: Long-form writing the business publishes: a guide, a policy, a report, terms and conditions.

files.api/make.yaml:
# THE DOCUMENT'S MAKE FUNCTION (docs/unoverse/data/objects/README.md 4b), private: only the
# pipeline runs it, once per file. Four steps, each one job, so a store can be swapped for another
# without touching the reading (owner, 2026-09-15): GET the file, PARSE it on the platform's own
# document service (docs/unoverse/data/documents/README.md), read what needs a second look with a
# vision model, and SAVE the reading beside the file, in its own folder under `_parsed/`. The
# parse says what to save by name; this says where. The one model call that names the document
# reads its first two pages and its outline, never its whole text.

description: Get the file, parse it, read its pictures, save the reading beside it.
calls:
  - name: get
    node: S3FileContent
    config:
      bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
      key: "{{ row.content.key }}"
      includeContent: false
  - name: parse
    node: ParseDocument
    config:
      fileUrl: "{{ calls.get.file.downloadUrl }}"
      fileName: "return String(row.content.key).split('/').at(-1)"
      includeFigures: true
      ocr: true
    # WHICH FILE THIS IS, so a parse already done is not done again. The node declares its own
    # memory (`cacheable: { ignore: [fileUrl], key: [etag] }`): the link is transport and changes
    # on every listing, the etag is the file. Handed nothing to key on, the engine refuses to
    # remember rather than remember wrongly (NodeMemoization.ts), and this call handed it nothing:
    # measured 2026-09-19, twenty-four parses in one run, none served from memory, eight files
    # parsed two and three times over.
    inputs:
      etag: "return String((calls.get.file && calls.get.file.etag) || row.content.etag || '')"
  # A SECOND READ OF WHAT NEEDS ONE (docs/unoverse/data/documents/review.md): the tables that
  # failed a check and every chart, offered by the service already rendered and capped per
  # document. A vision model reads each picture into a title, a header and rows as printed.
  # Optional: a read that fails leaves the parse as it was.
  - name: vision
    node: OpenAIStructuredOutput
    for: "return calls.parse.review || []"
    optional: true
    # READ ONCE PER PICTURE, NOT ONCE PER RUN (2026-09-20). A model call is not remembered by
    # default and that default is right: a prompt and a model are a caller's, and a completion
    # is not a lookup. THIS call is narrower than that. Its prompt is fixed here, its model is
    # named here, and what it is given is a PICTURE cut from a page that cannot change, named by
    # the hash of its own bytes. Asking the same question of the same picture twice costs the
    # same money and the same seconds for the same answer.
    #
    # Measured: reading fifteen documents spent about twelve minutes on these, and every one of
    # them was paid again on each re-read of the same unchanged files.
    cacheable:
      ignore: [content]
      key: [pictureHash]
    inputs:
      # WHAT THIS PICTURE IS. The parse names every region it offers for a read by the SHA-256
      # of the PNG it rendered, so the same picture is the same key whatever document, run or
      # machine it came from.
      pictureHash: "return String(item.hash || '')"
    config:
      # THE MODEL IS NAMED, never left to a default (owner, 2026-09-14).
      model: gpt-5.6-luna
      instructions: >-
        You read one picture of a table or a chart taken from a document. Return its title as
        printed, or a short plain title when none is printed; its column names, left to right;
        and every row, each cell exactly as printed, numbers with their signs, brackets, units
        and percent signs. For a chart, return one row per category or date and one column per
        series, with the values its labels print. Leave a value the chart does not label empty;
        never estimate it.
      schemaName: table_picture
      reasoning: none
      content: "return { type: 'image', imageUrl: 'data:image/png;base64,' + item.image_png_base64, metadata: { kind: item.kind, page: item.page } }"
      schema:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [title, header, rows]
        properties:
          title:
            type: string
            description: The title as printed, or a short plain one.
          header:
            type: array
            description: The column names, left to right.
            items:
              type: string
          rows:
            type: array
            description: Every row, each cell exactly as printed.
            items:
              type: array
              items:
                type: string
  # THE READING, SAVED BESIDE THE FILE (ruled 2026-09-11; one folder per document since
  # 2026-09-15): what the parse says to save, and what the vision read found in a picture, a
  # table's rows or a chart's values, in place of the parse's rows for that table.
  - name: save
    node: S3Upload
    for: >-
      return (() => {
        const review = calls.parse.review || [];
        const read = (id) => { const k = review.findIndex(r => r.id === id); const v = k >= 0 && calls.vision && calls.vision[k] ? calls.vision[k].result : null; return v && Array.isArray(v.rows) && v.rows.length && (() => { const cells = v.rows.flatMap(r => Array.isArray(r) ? r.slice(1) : []); return cells.length > 0 && cells.filter(x => String(x == null ? '' : x).trim()).length * 2 >= cells.length; })() ? v : null; };
        const seen = review.map(r => ({ r: r, v: read(r.id) })).filter(x => x.v);
        const replaced = seen.map(x => 'tables/' + x.r.id + '.json');
        return (calls.parse.files || []).filter(f => !replaced.includes(f.name))
          .concat(seen.map(x => ({ name: 'tables/' + x.r.id + '.json', contentType: 'application/json', text: JSON.stringify({ id: x.r.id, caption: x.v.title || null, header: [x.v.header || []], rows: x.v.rows, readBy: 'vision' }) })));
      })()
    config:
      bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
      key: "return String(row.content.key).split('/').slice(0, -1).concat(['_parsed', String(row.content.key).split('/').at(-1), item.name]).join('/')"
      sourceType: "return item.base64 ? 'base64' : 'text'"
      textData: "return item.base64 ? undefined : String(item.text || '')"
      base64Data: "return item.base64 || undefined"
      contentType: "{{ item.contentType }}"
  # WHAT A STANDARDISED DOCUMENT SAYS ABOUT ITSELF, AND THE FIGURES IT STATES
  # (../../../../../docs/unoverse/data/documents/README.md, ruled 2026-09-18, made one call
  # 2026-09-19), where the read was handed a layout that describes this kind of document.
  #
  # ONE PASS OVER A FILE, NOT TWO. This used to be two: a cover read that opened every file in the
  # folder before any of them was read, to take two cells off each, and then this. Nothing needed
  # the first one early: what it read is used when the row is written and when its lines are drawn,
  # both of which happen after the parse. So it cost a second download of every file, a wait before
  # any document could start (measured 110 seconds for fifteen), and a join back onto the file it
  # came from, which was silently wrong for months. The layout says where a document keeps its name,
  # its date and its figures; all three are read here, from the parse, in one call.
  # Deterministic: no model, no second parse, and never the file again. A layout says which sheets
  # hold figures and which column holds which measure; it knows nothing of any industry, and the
  # layouts are the caller's, as the cover read's are.
  #
  # FROM WHAT THE PARSE ALREADY HOLDS, in memory, not fetched back from the store it was just
  # saved to. A parse keeps what a document PRINTS, and the workbook beneath a cell printing
  # 1.838% holds 0.01838; measured 2026-09-17, reading the file instead put the long column's
  # figure under short, scaled by a hundredth, and nothing about it looked wrong.
  #
  # Skipped entirely when no layout was handed to the read, which is every document by default.
  - name: values
    node: ReadValues
    when: "return ((row.content.layouts || row.content.valueTemplates || []).length > 0)"
    optional: true
    config:
      documents: >-
        return [{
          file_name: String(row.content.key || '').split('/').at(-1),
          subject: row.content.coverSubject || null,
          period: row.content.coverPeriod || null,
          text: String(calls.parse.firstPages || ''),
          tables: (() => {
            const review = calls.parse.review || [];
            const read = (id) => { const k = review.findIndex(r => r.id === id); const v = k >= 0 && calls.vision && calls.vision[k] ? calls.vision[k].result : null; return v && Array.isArray(v.rows) && v.rows.length ? v : null; };
            const seen = review.map(r => ({ r: r, v: read(r.id) })).filter(x => x.v);
            const replaced = seen.map(x => 'tables/' + x.r.id + '.json');
            const parsed = (calls.parse.files || [])
              .filter(f => String(f.name || '').indexOf('tables/') === 0 && !replaced.includes(f.name) && String(f.text || '').trim().indexOf('{') === 0)
              .map(f => JSON.parse(f.text))
              .filter(t => t && Array.isArray(t.rows));
            return parsed.concat(seen.map(x => ({ id: x.r.id, caption: x.v.title || null, header: [x.v.header || []], rows: x.v.rows })));
          })()
        }]
      templates: "return row.content.layouts || row.content.valueTemplates || []"
returns:
  # THE DOCUMENT NAMES ITSELF (owner, 2026-09-10; moved from the pipelines 2026-09-15): the file's
  # name without its extensions, as a person reads it ("WM Summary", never "WM Summary.docx.pdf").
  title: >-
    return String(row.content.title || String(row.content.key || '').split('/').at(-1))
      .split('.').filter((p, i, a) => i === 0 || a.slice(i).some(q => !['pdf', 'docx', 'pptx', 'xlsx', 'xlsm', 'md', 'txt', 'doc', 'ppt', 'xls', 'csv'].includes(q.toLowerCase()))).join('.')
  # THE TEXT THE MODEL READS (owner, 2026-09-14: "take the first two pages"): the first two
  # pages, then every heading with its first words, then the parts by id. The one model call
  # names the document, its sections (sectionNames) and its parts (partNames) from it.
  text: >-
    return '# ' + String(row.content.title || String(row.content.key || '').split('/').at(-1)) + '\n\n'
      + String(calls.parse.firstPages || '')
      + (String(calls.parse.firstPages || '').length < String(calls.parse.text || '').length ? '\n\n(The first two pages. The rest of the document is in its sections, headed below.)' : '')
      + (() => {
        const o = calls.parse.outline || [];
        return o.length > 1 ? '\n\n# Headings of this document\n\n' + o.map(x => '- ' + x.id + ' (page ' + (x.page || '') + '): ' + x.title + (x.firstWords ? ' | ' + x.firstWords : '')).join('\n') : '';
      })()
      + (() => {
        const p = calls.parse.parts || {};
        const tables = (p.tables || []).map(t => {
          const cols = (t.columns || []).filter(c => c).slice(0, 10).join(' | ');
          return '- ' + t.partId + ' (table, page ' + (t.page == null ? '' : t.page) + ')' + (t.caption ? ': ' + t.caption : '') + (cols ? '. Columns: ' + cols : '') + (t.firstRows ? '. First rows: ' + t.firstRows : '');
        });
        const figures = (p.figures || []).map(f => '- ' + f.partId + ' (' + f.kind + ', page ' + (f.page == null ? '' : f.page) + ')' + (f.caption ? ': ' + f.caption : ''));
        const all = tables.concat(figures).slice(0, 30);
        return all.length ? '\n\n# Parts of this document\n\n' + all.join('\n') : '';
      })()
  # WHAT THE DOCUMENT STATED ABOUT ITSELF, where it was read from a known place before this ran
  # (docs/unoverse/data/documents/arriving.md). Carried on the item by whoever collected it, and
  # passed through untouched: no model has seen these, and none should. Empty where nothing read
  # them, which is the honest answer and leaves the model's own reading to stand.
  # WHAT THE DOCUMENT STATED ABOUT ITSELF: read here from the place its layout names, or carried
  # on the item where whoever collected it read it first. No model has seen these, and none should.
  statedSubject: "return String(row.content.coverSubject || ((calls.values && calls.values.documents && calls.values.documents[0]) || {}).subject || '')"
  statedPeriod: "return String(row.content.coverPeriod || ((calls.values && calls.values.documents && calls.values.documents[0]) || {}).period || '')"
  statedType: "return String(((calls.values && calls.values.documents && calls.values.documents[0]) || {}).template || '')"
  statedWhere: "return String(row.content.coverFoundIn || ((calls.values && calls.values.documents && calls.values.documents[0]) || {}).found_in || '')"
  # WHETHER THE READ IS FINISHED, ON THE ROW (2026-09-22). The layout names the tables it wants;
  # the read is finished when every one of them was found and gave something. That is the whole
  # judgement, and it is the only one that scales: it is made from the layout, written once per
  # KIND of document, and never from the document in front of us. A table nobody asked for is not
  # a failure and is not counted as one. The four figure counts below say how much of the document
  # any layout reaches at all, which is a fact about the layout's ambition, not a mark out of ten.
  figuresCells: "return Number(((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).cells || 0)"
  figuresSaying: "return Number(((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).saying || 0)"
  figuresRead: "return Number(((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).read || 0)"
  figuresTook: "return Number(((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).took || 0)"
  tablesAsked: "return Number(((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).asked || 0)"
  tablesMissing: "return (((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).missing || []).length"
  tablesMissingNames: >-
    return (((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).missing || []).slice(0, 20)
  figuresElsewhere: >-
    return (((((calls.values || {}).documents || [])[0] || {}).coverage || {}).elsewhere || [])
      .reduce((n, u) => n + Number(u.saying || 0), 0)
  pages: "{{ calls.parse.document.pages }}"
  bucket: "{{ row.content.bucket }}"
  key: "{{ row.content.key }}"
  parsedKey: "return String(row.content.key).split('/').slice(0, -1).concat(['_parsed', String(row.content.key).split('/').at(-1), 'text.md']).join('/')"
  structureKey: "return String(row.content.key).split('/').slice(0, -1).concat(['_parsed', String(row.content.key).split('/').at(-1), 'structure.json']).join('/')"
  # THE PARTS (pipelines README, make, parts): the parse's tables, with what a vision read found
  # in place of what the text gave; and a chart the vision read into rows, a table of its own, its
  # picture the evidence. CELLS MEAN VALUES (owner, 2026-09-12): a read counts only when at least
  # half its value cells hold one.
  tables: >-
    return (() => {
      const review = calls.parse.review || [];
      const read = (id) => { const k = review.findIndex(r => r.id === id); const v = k >= 0 && calls.vision && calls.vision[k] ? calls.vision[k].result : null; return v && Array.isArray(v.rows) && v.rows.length && (() => { const cells = v.rows.flatMap(r => Array.isArray(r) ? r.slice(1) : []); return cells.length > 0 && cells.filter(x => String(x == null ? '' : x).trim()).length * 2 >= cells.length; })() ? v : null; };
      const base = String(row.content.key).split('/').slice(0, -1).concat(['_parsed', String(row.content.key).split('/').at(-1)]).join('/') + '/';
      const VISION = { read_by: 'vision', cells_in_text: null, totals_checked: 0, totals_agree: 0, review: ['read from a picture by a vision model'] };
      const p = calls.parse.parts || {};
      const tables = (p.tables || []).map(t => {
        const v = read(t.partId);
        const columns = v ? (v.header || []).map(x => String(x || '')) : (t.columns || []);
        const named = columns.filter(c => c);
        const rows = v ? v.rows.length : t.rowCount;
        return {
          partId: t.partId,
          title: t.caption || (v && v.title) || t.title,
          description: rows + ' rows' + (named.length ? '; columns: ' + named.slice(0, 10).join(', ') : ''),
          page: t.page, box: t.box, columns: columns, rowCount: rows, stitchedFrom: t.stitchedFrom,
          checks: v ? VISION : t.checks,
          bucket: row.content.bucket, structureKey: base + 'structure.json', rowsKey: base + t.rowsFile,
          pictureKey: t.pictureFile ? base + t.pictureFile : null
        };
      });
      const charts = (p.figures || [])
        .filter(f => review.some(r => r.id === f.partId && r.kind === 'chart'))
        .map(f => ({ f: f, v: read(f.partId) })).filter(x => x.v)
        .map(x => {
          const f = x.f;
          const v = x.v;
          const columns = (v.header || []).map(x => String(x || ''));
          const named = columns.filter(c => c);
          return {
            partId: f.partId,
            title: f.caption || v.title || ('Table, page ' + f.page),
            description: v.rows.length + ' rows' + (named.length ? '; columns: ' + named.slice(0, 10).join(', ') : '') + '; read from a picture by a vision model',
            page: f.page, box: f.box, columns: columns, rowCount: v.rows.length, checks: VISION,
            bucket: row.content.bucket, structureKey: base + 'structure.json', rowsKey: base + 'tables/' + f.partId + '.json',
            pictureKey: f.pictureFile ? base + f.pictureFile : null
          };
        });
      return tables.concat(charts);
    })()
  # What stays a picture: a meaningful figure the vision read found no rows in.
  figures: >-
    return (() => {
      const review = calls.parse.review || [];
      const read = (id) => { const k = review.findIndex(r => r.id === id); const v = k >= 0 && calls.vision && calls.vision[k] ? calls.vision[k].result : null; return v && Array.isArray(v.rows) && v.rows.length && (() => { const cells = v.rows.flatMap(r => Array.isArray(r) ? r.slice(1) : []); return cells.length > 0 && cells.filter(x => String(x == null ? '' : x).trim()).length * 2 >= cells.length; })() ? v : null; };
      const base = String(row.content.key).split('/').slice(0, -1).concat(['_parsed', String(row.content.key).split('/').at(-1)]).join('/') + '/';
      return ((calls.parse.parts || {}).figures || [])
        .filter(f => !(review.some(r => r.id === f.partId && r.kind === 'chart') && read(f.partId)))
        .map(f => ({ partId: f.partId, title: f.title, description: f.description, kind: f.kind, page: f.page, box: f.box, bucket: row.content.bucket, key: row.content.key, pictureKey: f.pictureFile ? base + f.pictureFile : null }));
    })()
  # THE FIGURES THIS DOCUMENT STATED, one row per figure, each proved against what the document
  # states about itself. A part of the document like its tables and its figures, and written into
  # the table its object owns (../../../../../docs/unoverse/data/objects/dataset.md). Empty for a
  # document of no layout we know, which is the honest answer and is not a failure.
  # A DOCUMENT THAT COULD NOT PROVE ITSELF SAYS NOTHING, IT DOES NOT SAY "NOTHING". An empty
  # list means this document states no figures any more, and what it stated before is removed;
  # a refused read means we do not know what it states, and what was stored must stand. Those
  # are different answers and only one of them is a list. Measured 2026-09-19: a check refused
  # one sheet, the read offered nothing, and four hundred and eighty figures already stored were
  # deleted as though the document had withdrawn them.
  readings: >-
    return (() => {
      const v = calls.values;
      if (!v) return [];
      if ((v.unproven || []).length) return null;
      return v.readings || [];
    })()
  dates: "{{ calls.parse.document.dates }}"
  scanned: "{{ calls.parse.document.scanned }}"
  # THE READER IT WAS READ WITH (pipelines README, One row per item): a new parser reads it again.
  parsedWith: "{{ calls.parse.document.parser_version }}"
  # WHAT THE READER HAD TO WORK AROUND, said on the row and on its inbox line (2026-09-13).
  readWarnings: "return (calls.parse.quality && Array.isArray(calls.parse.quality.warnings)) ? calls.parse.quality.warnings : []"
files.document.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# Long-form content the business publishes (Content, docs/unoverse/data/objects/elements/content.md),
# placed whole by what it is about: a guide, an article, a report. Many per source, since a
# document answers several needs. The base plus one field of its own, the summary, written
# from the file read whole: api/service.yaml fetches the file's link and parses it, and the
# summary prop pulls that function (README 4b, 5).
type: object
name: document
# THE GLYPH its rows are drawn with (README 4a): a lucide icon name.
icon: file-text
extends: need
uniqueBy: [source_url, title]
embed: [title, description, key_need, related_needs, questions, callToAction]
search: [universal_id, object_type, title, description, key_need, source_url, source_id]
meta: open

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it: what this is and when an Agent reaches for it.
title: Document
description: >-
  Long-form writing the business publishes: a guide, a policy, a report, terms and conditions.
whenToUse: >-
  What do the terms say? What does the report say about this? Where is this written down? Show me the policy.
category: Objects
version: 1.0.0

# THE LINES A DOCUMENT DRAWS TO ANOTHER (docs/unoverse/data/objects/relationships-and-labels.md):
# among the documents of one folder, drawn again whenever one of them is written. An issue of a
# series follows the issue before it and both stay true for their date; a new version of a
# memorandum, agreement, policy, deck or questionnaire replaces the one before it, and current
# is the one nothing replaces (docs/unoverse/data/README.md, "series and versions are different words").
# The names are written by each document's own read, so one thing may be named several ways:
# `alike` asks, once per folder, which names are the same. A series is one subject's: two companies
# may both issue a "quarterly review", and one never follows the other's.
links:
  follows:
    type: flow
    between: [subject, series]
    alike: [subject, series]
    order: asOf
    when: "return !!row.series"
  replaces:
    type: flow
    between: [kind, subject]
    alike: [subject]
    order: asOf
    when: "return !row.series && ['presentation', 'questionnaire', 'memorandum', 'agreement', 'policy'].includes(row.kind)"

props: { $include: props }
files.props.yaml:
# A DOCUMENT'S OWN FIELDS. Everything else it carries is the need's (objects/need/props.yaml).
# THE PROP IS THE BRIEF (UNOVERSE_AUTHORING.md 3b): the description is the whole instruction.
# Written from the file read whole, so it says `from: make.text` (README 4b: the prop
# pulls the function); the six positioning fields are written from the same read.
# THE TITLE IS THE DOCUMENT'S NAME (owner, 2026-09-10: the inbox showed "Assess the legal risks
# of..." where the file was the legal DD summary). Like a product, a document re-briefs the
# need's title: the essence stays a need, the name stays the document's.
title:
  description: >-
    The document's own name, as its first page or its file name gives it, with what it is
    about and its date when the document prints them and the name does not already carry
    them: "Employee Handbook", "Supplier Agreement, Northwind Ltd, 1 March 2026". Never the
    bare file name when the document names itself, and never a title that could belong to
    another document of the same kind about another subject. A name, never an outcome
    phrase; the outcome is the key need.
summary:
  type: string
  input: true
  from: make.text
  description: >-
    What a reader learns from this document, in the document's own terms: its subject, what
    it covers and what it concludes or provides, three to six sentences. Only what the text
    says, never an assessment of it. Plain text.
  maxLength: 1200
# WHAT KIND OF DOCUMENT, ABOUT WHAT, AS OF WHEN (docs/unoverse/data/README.md step 4): written
# by the same read as the summary, never a second call. They are what the document's `links`
# (document.yaml) draw its lines from: a letter follows the letter before it, a policy replaces
# the one it supersedes.
kind:
  type: string
  input: true
  from: make.text
  enum: [letter, report, factsheet, commentary, presentation, questionnaire, memorandum, supplement, agreement, policy, financial-statements, meeting-notes, form, other]
  description: >-
    What kind of document this is, by what it is, never by what it is about. letter: a
    periodic letter to its readers. report: a periodic report of figures or activity.
    factsheet: a short periodic summary of figures. commentary: a periodic comment on what
    happened. presentation: a deck. questionnaire: questions and their answers, such as a survey
    or an application. memorandum: a formal document setting out terms or information for its
    readers. supplement: a
    document that amends another. agreement: a contract. policy: a stated policy or procedure.
    financial-statements: accounts, audited or not. meeting-notes: notes of a meeting. form:
    a form to fill in. other: none of these.
subject:
  type: string
  input: true
  from: make.text
  reuse: true
  maxLength: 80
  description: >-
    What the document is about, as a name: the company, product, project or policy it concerns,
    in the fewest words. Two documents about the same thing give the same subject, so give
    the name, never a description of the document. Two things that are distinct in law or in
    form, such as two entities with different legal names, are different subjects however
    close their names.
series:
  type: string
  input: true
  from: make.text
  reuse: true
  maxLength: 80
  description: >-
    The regular series this document is one issue of, as a name: the same kind of document,
    about the same subject, issued again and again (a monthly report, a quarterly letter,
    annual accounts). Empty when the document is not one issue of a series, such as a
    memorandum, an agreement, a presentation or a questionnaire.
asOf:
  type: string
  input: true
  from: make.text
  maxLength: 10
  description: >-
    The date the document speaks as of, as YYYY-MM-DD: the date its figures are stated at, or
    when it has none, the date it was issued. Only a date the document gives; empty when it
    gives none.
# WHERE THE BODY IS (owner ruling 2026-09-10: "the document row should be like other objects;
# it extends need, which captures the essence"). The row holds the essence and a summary; the
# parsed text lives in the store, beside the source under the reserved `_parsed/` folder,
# and getDetail serves it. These three say where, written straight from the function
# (input: false, from: make.*), never through the model.
# WHAT THE DOCUMENT ITSELF STATED, read from a known place before the document was read at all
# (docs/unoverse/data/documents/arriving.md, ruled 2026-09-18). A document that comes on a
# template says what it is about and the date it speaks as of in a fixed cell or a fixed place on
# its cover, and taking them from there is exact where reading them is a judgement. These three
# say what was taken and where it was taken from, written straight from the function
# (input: false), never through the model, and empty where nothing read them: `subject` and
# `asOf` above are the reading, and stand on their own when these are empty.
statedSubject:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.statedSubject
  description: >-
    What the document states it is about, taken from the place its template keeps it. The
    document's own words, never inferred from where the file sat or what it was called.
statedPeriod:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.statedPeriod
  description: >-
    The date the document states it speaks as of, as YYYY-MM-DD, taken from the place its
    template keeps it, never from the file name.
statedType:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.statedType
  description: >-
    The layout that recognised this document, by its name. A standardised document is known by a
    marker in a fixed place, so this is what the document IS, settled with no model and no guess
    from its file name. Empty for a document no layout we hold recognised, which is the honest
    answer: we do not know what it is.
statedWhere:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.statedWhere
  description: >-
    Where the two above were read, in words a person can check ("subject: 1. Details, row 1",
    "period: page 1 (read by OCR)"). A stated fact that cannot say where it came from is a
    guess wearing a better name.
# WHETHER THE READ IS FINISHED, AND HOW MUCH OF THE DOCUMENT IT REACHES. Two different
# questions, and only the first is a judgement. The layout names the tables it wants, so the
# read is finished when it got all of them (`tablesMissing` is zero) and short when it did not.
# The figure counts are the second question: a plain measure of how much of the document any
# layout touches at all. A table nobody asked for is not a failure and is never counted as one.
figuresCells:
  type: number
  input: false
  from: make.figuresCells
  description: How many numbered cells this document held, across every table its parse found.
figuresSaying:
  type: number
  input: false
  from: make.figuresSaying
  description: >-
    How many of those say anything at all: a number that is not zero. A standard's return prints
    every sheet whether the fund uses it or not, so counting cells alone makes the largest thing
    we never read a sheet of a thousand zeros. This is the number to judge by.
figuresRead:
  type: number
  input: false
  from: make.figuresRead
  description: >-
    How many readings the document made, counting every one. The gap from `figuresCells` is not
    all loss and must not be read as one: a table's own total is deliberately not a slicing of
    it, a column the layout does not name is a column we do not want, and a block that could not
    prove itself is refused on purpose.
figuresTook:
  type: number
  input: false
  from: make.figuresTook
  description: >-
    How many of the readings say something: a figure that is not zero. THE ONE TO PUT BESIDE
    `figuresSaying`, because those two count the same thing on both sides. `figuresRead` counts
    the zeros and `figuresSaying` does not, so read-over-saying was never a share of anything:
    measured 2026-09-22, one document came out at 228% and would have been drawn as a full bar.
figuresElsewhere:
  type: number
  input: false
  from: make.figuresElsewhere
  description: >-
    The figures, saying something, that sit in tables no block of the layout asked for. NOT a
    miss and never drawn as one: a set of audited accounts holds its portfolio position by
    position and its accounting plumbing, wanted by nobody, and counted as a miss they made a
    document that had been read perfectly well report 2%.
tablesAsked:
  type: number
  input: false
  from: make.tablesAsked
  description: How many tables this document's layout named, counting every block.
tablesMissing:
  type: number
  input: false
  from: make.tablesMissing
  description: >-
    How many of those the document did not give: no table answered to the name, or the one that
    did gave nothing back. THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES whether a read is finished. Zero is finished,
    however little of the document the layout wanted; above zero is short, however much it read.
tablesMissingNames:
  type: array
  input: false
  from: make.tablesMissingNames
  description: Those tables by the name the layout asked for, so a person can go and look.
  items:
    type: string
    description: One table the layout named and the document did not give.
bucket:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.bucket
  description: The bucket the file and its parsed text sit in.
key:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.key
  description: The file's key in the bucket.
parsedKey:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.parsedKey
  description: The key of the parsed text, under the file's folder in `_parsed/`, kept by the make function.
structureKey:
  type: string
  input: false
  from: make.structureKey
  description: The key of the document's structure (sections with their text, tables with their rows, figures, lists, dates), under the file's folder in `_parsed/`, kept by the make function.
readWarnings:
  type: array
  input: false
  from: make.readWarnings
  description: >-
    What the document service had to work around to read the file, in its words: pages with no
    text layer or with text that cannot be read, read from their image instead; a document that
    could not be read at all. Shown on the file's inbox line, so a file is never read as nothing
    without saying so.
  items:
    type: string

partNames:
  type: array
  input: true
  from: make.text
  description: >-
    A name for each part listed under "Parts of this document" at the end of the text: each
    table and figure the document holds, by its id. Write for someone deciding whether to open
    it without seeing it. The title says what the part shows, in the document's own terms (a
    table of prices by region, not "Table 1"). The description says what it holds
    and over what period or scope. When to use says the question it answers. Only parts in
    that list, by the id it gives; never a part it does not list.
  maxItems: 30
  items:
    partId:
      type: string
      description: The part's id exactly as the list gives it, such as t2 or f5.
      maxLength: 12
    title:
      type: string
      description: What the part shows, in a few words, in the document's own terms.
      maxLength: 90
    description:
      type: string
      description: What it holds and over what period or scope, in one sentence.
      maxLength: 180
    whenToUse:
      type: string
      description: The question it answers, in one sentence, as a reader would ask it.
      maxLength: 140
# THE DOCUMENT'S SECTIONS (owner, 2026-09-13: "Two different things"; objects/README.md,
# "Sections and relationships are two different things"): its contents, named by the same one
# read that names its parts. A section is not a row: it is a run of the structure file's
# headings, from the one it starts at to the next section's start, and it carries a face.
sectionNames:
  type: array
  input: true
  from: make.text
  description: >-
    The document's sections, as its table of contents would list them. Under "Headings of this
    document" at the end of the text is every heading the file has, by its id and page, in
    order, each with its section's first words after a bar; many are small or repeated. Group them into the document's real sections: each
    starts at one heading and runs to the next section's start, in the document's order, and
    together they cover the document. Write for someone deciding whether to open a section
    without seeing it. The title says what the section covers, in the document's own terms.
    The description says what it holds, in one sentence. When to use says the question it
    answers. Only headings in that list, by the id it gives. None when the list is absent.
  maxItems: 30
  items:
    startsAt:
      type: string
      description: The id of the heading the section starts at, exactly as the list gives it, such as s12.
      maxLength: 12
    title:
      type: string
      description: What the section covers, in a few words, in the document's own terms.
      maxLength: 90
    description:
      type: string
      description: What it holds, in one sentence.
      maxLength: 180
    whenToUse:
      type: string
      description: The question it answers, in one sentence, as a reader would ask it.
      maxLength: 140
files.test.yaml:
# THE OBJECT UNDER GUARD: the nodes make names faked, the returns asserted. The item is a file the
# bucket pipeline put in the inbox, carried as listed: the file got, one parse on the document
# service (ParseDocument) that says what to save by name, one save beside the file in its own
# folder under `_parsed/`, one text for the model (the first two pages, the outline, the parts),
# and the tables and meaningful figures as parts: the logo never, the chart with where it sits
# and no bytes. The service offers a flagged table and two charts for a vision read: the table's
# part carries the read's columns, a chart read into rows is a table part, and only a chart with
# no rows stays an image. What the model writes from the text is not faked here.
testData:
  row:
    source: bucket
    sourceUrl: s3://example-docs/guides/onboarding.pdf
    sourceId: 3f1a9c2b7d4e
    suggested: document
    content:
      coverSubject: Example Onboarding Programme
      coverPeriod: "2026-07-31"
      coverFoundIn: "subject: page 1"
      # A LAYOUT WAS HANDED TO THIS READ, so its figures are read from the tables the parse kept.
      # A document carrying none skips the call entirely and states no figures.
      valueTemplates:
        - name: onboarding
          match: Onboarding
          observations:
            - sheets: [Fees]
              measures: [{ measure: fee, unit: percent_of_aum }]
      title: onboarding.pdf
      bucket: example-docs
      key: guides/onboarding.pdf
      handler: make
  fake:
    get:
      file: { key: guides/onboarding.pdf, bucket: example-docs, size: 812345, universalId: 3f1a9c2b7d4e, downloadUrl: "https://example-docs.s3.amazonaws.com/guides/onboarding.pdf?sig=1", content: "" }
    parse:
      document: { title: Onboarding, pages: 4, kind: pdf, scanned: false, dates: [{ text: "31 July 2026", iso: "2026-07-31", where: footer, page: 1 }], content_hash: abc123, parser_version: docling-2.126.0 }
      text: "# Onboarding\n\nHow a new customer opens an account in three steps."
      firstPages: "# Onboarding\n\nHow a new customer opens an account in three steps."
      outline: [{ id: s1, page: 1, title: Onboarding, firstWords: "" }]
      review: [{ id: t2, kind: table, reasons: [read from a picture by OCR], page: 3, image_png_base64: CCCC }, { id: f2, kind: chart, reasons: ["a chart: its values read as a table"], page: 3, image_png_base64: BBBB }, { id: f3, kind: chart, reasons: ["a chart: its values read as a table"], page: 4, image_png_base64: DDDD }]
      parts:
        tables:
          - { partId: t1, title: "Table, page 2 (Step, Owner)", caption: null, description: "2 rows; columns: Step, Owner", page: 2, box: null, columns: [Step, Owner], rowCount: 2, firstRows: "Open the form | Customer / Verify identity | Bank", stitchedFrom: null, checks: { read_by: text, cells_in_text: 1, totals_checked: 0, totals_agree: 0, review: [] }, rowsFile: tables/t1.json, pictureFile: pictures/t1.png }
          - { partId: t2, title: Fees, caption: Fees, description: "1 rows; columns: Fee, Rate", page: 3, box: null, columns: [Fee, Rate], rowCount: 1, firstRows: "Annual | 1%", stitchedFrom: null, checks: null, rowsFile: tables/t2.json, pictureFile: pictures/t2.png }
        figures:
          - { partId: f2, title: Accounts opened by month, caption: Accounts opened by month, description: "chart on page 3: Accounts opened by month", kind: chart, page: 3, box: { x0: 72, y0: 300, x1: 300, y1: 420 }, pictureFile: pictures/f2.png }
          - { partId: f3, title: "chart, page 4", caption: null, description: chart on page 4, kind: chart, page: 4, box: null, pictureFile: pictures/f3.png }
      files: [{ name: text.md, contentType: text/markdown, text: x }, { name: structure.json, contentType: application/json, text: "{}" }, { name: tables/t1.json, contentType: application/json, text: "{}" }, { name: tables/t2.json, contentType: application/json, text: "{}" }, { name: pictures/t1.png, contentType: image/png, base64: TTTT }, { name: pictures/t2.png, contentType: image/png, base64: UUUU }, { name: pictures/f2.png, contentType: image/png, base64: BBBB }, { name: pictures/f3.png, contentType: image/png, base64: DDDD }]
      quality: { warnings: [] }
    vision:
      - result: { title: Fees, header: [Fee, Rate, Basis], rows: [[Annual, "1%", Assets]] }
      - result: { title: Accounts opened by month, header: [Month, Accounts], rows: [[Jan, "120"], [Feb, "140"]] }
      - result: { title: Wait times, header: [Quarter, Days, Target, Industry], rows: [[Q1, "4", "", ""], [Q2, "6", "", ""], [Q3, "5", "", ""]] }
    save:
      - output: { key: guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/text.md, bucket: example-docs }
    values:
      readings: [{ fund: Example, measure: fee, value: 1, unit: percent_of_aum, as_of: "2026-07-31", scope: whole, basis: reported, source: "Fees, row 1" }]
      documents: [{ file_name: onboarding.pdf, template: onboarding, ok: true, readings: 1 }]
      total: 1
  expect:
    text: "return output.text.startsWith('# onboarding.pdf') && output.text.includes('three steps') && output.text.includes('# Parts of this document') && output.text.includes('- t1 (table, page 2). Columns: Step | Owner') && output.text.includes('- f2 (chart, page 3): Accounts opened by month') && !output.text.includes('- f1 ')"
    title: "return output.title === 'onboarding'"
    pages: "return output.pages === 4"
    saved: "return output.parsedKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/text.md' && output.bucket === 'example-docs' && output.key === 'guides/onboarding.pdf'"
    read: "return output.read === 'make'"
    structure: "return output.structureKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/structure.json' && output.dates[0].iso === '2026-07-31'"
    tables: "return output.tables.length === 3 && output.tables[1].title === 'Fees' && output.tables[1].rowsKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/tables/t2.json' && output.tables[0].partId === 't1' && output.tables[0].rowCount === 2 && output.tables[0].columns.join(',') === 'Step,Owner' && output.tables[0].structureKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/structure.json' && output.tables[0].rowsKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/tables/t1.json' && output.tables[0].page === 2"
    figures: "return output.figures.length === 1 && output.figures[0].partId === 'f3' && output.figures[0].kind === 'chart' && output.figures[0].key === 'guides/onboarding.pdf' && output.figures[0].image_png_base64 === undefined && output.figures[0].rowsKey === undefined"
    checks: "return output.tables[0].checks.read_by === 'text' && output.tables[1].checks.read_by === 'vision' && output.tables[1].columns.join(',') === 'Fee,Rate,Basis' && output.tables[1].rowCount === 1"
    chart: "return output.tables.some(c => c.partId === 'f2' && c.rowsKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/tables/f2.json' && c.rowCount === 2 && c.checks.read_by === 'vision' && c.title === 'Accounts opened by month' && c.box.x0 === 72 && c.pictureKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/pictures/f2.png') && !output.figures.some(f => f.partId === 'f2') && output.figures[0].title === 'chart, page 4'"
    parsedWith: "return output.parsedWith === 'docling-2.126.0'"
    # WHAT THE DOCUMENT STATED comes through untouched, and no model is on that path.
    stated: "return output.statedSubject === 'Example Onboarding Programme' && output.statedPeriod === '2026-07-31' && output.statedWhere === 'subject: page 1'"
    # THE FIGURES THE DOCUMENT STATED, a part like its tables and its figures, read from the
    # parse's own tables and never from the file again.
    readings: "return output.readings.length === 1 && output.readings[0].measure === 'fee' && output.readings[0].unit === 'percent_of_aum'"
    pictures: "return output.figures[0].pictureKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/pictures/f3.png' && output.tables[1].pictureKey === 'guides/_parsed/onboarding.pdf/pictures/t2.png'"
